case_name: Dale W. Laue and Alicia Laue v. Commissioner

taxpayer.notes: Dale Laue separated from Rockwell in 1987 (B-1B program); generally unemployed since 2002 at age 46.

adjustments: 10% additional tax under section 72(t) of $2,517 on Boeing pension lump-sum distribution
conceded: Petitioners: no general hardship exception to §72(t); no other exception argued

findings_of_fact.fact: Worked for Rockwell on B-1B program until 1987 (separation from service)
findings_of_fact.snippet: He worked for Rockwell International (Rockwell) on the B-1B bomber program until 1987.

findings_of_fact.fact: Generally unemployed since 2002 when he was 46
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner has been generally unemployed since 2002, when he was 46 years old.

findings_of_fact.fact: Lump-sum gross distribution of $25,170 from Boeing pension deposited November 14, 2015
findings_of_fact.snippet: deposited the lump-sum gross distribution of $25,170 on November 14, 2015
At the time of distribution and deposit petitioner was 59 years old but had not yet attained the age of 59-1/2.

findings_of_fact.fact: Distribution reported as income ($32,250 total pensions incl. $7,080 Northrop Grumman SEPP not in issue) but no 10% additional tax reported
findings_of_fact.snippet: they did not include the 10% additional tax pursuant to section 72(t)(1).

findings_of_fact.fact: Notice of deficiency issued November 27, 2017 for $2,517 additional tax
findings_of_fact.snippet: the 10% additional tax of $2,517 because they received the Boeing distribution before petitioner attained age 59-1/2

issues.question: Are petitioners liable for the 10% additional tax under §72(t) on the $25,170 Boeing pension distribution, or does the §72(t)(2)(A)(v) separation-after-age-55 exception apply?
provisions: H.R. Conf. Rept. No. 99-841 (Vol. II), at II-456 to II-457
issues.holding: Liable: exception requires attaining age 55 on or before separation from service; petitioner separated from Rockwell in 1987 well before age 55 and was under 59-1/2 at distribution
issues.computable_reason: Mechanical: age at separation (<55) and age at distribution (<59.5) vs statutory exceptions; 10% x $25,170.

decision.text: Decision will be entered for respondent.

notes: Birth date not stated; age at 1987 separation derived (from age 46 in 2002) as about 31 (derived). Statutory interpretation: separation must occur in or after the year employee attains 55 (court relied on conference report). 10% of $25,170 = $2,517 (rounded).
